evidence: The paper uses ranger random forest models "weighted for class imbalance and tuned to 500 trees, up to 3 variables to split each node on and maximum tree depth of 20" for imputation, evaluating performance through cross-validation confusion matrices: "Model 2, constrained to the number of subdistricts predicted by model 1, correctly guessed ≈80% of the true subdistricts of origin and ≈63% of true subdistricts of arrival." No variable importance scores are reported or interpreted. All substantive conclusions concern population estimates ("Yemen's population rose from about 26.3 M to 31.1 M during the seven-year analysis period") derived from the imputed dataset and sensitivity analyses on key parameters.
